decisions.choice: the second year after the exodus, in the wilderness of Sinai: the book begins where Exodus and Leviticus leave Israel
decisions.reason: Israel reached the wilderness of Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exodus 19:1), and the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year (Exodus 40:17). Since then the LORD has spoken to Moses from the tent of meeting (Leviticus 1:1). One month later he orders this count of the men who can fight, to prepare the people for the march. They leave Sinai on the twentieth day of this same month (10:11), and the book follows them through the wilderness to the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho (22:1; 36:13).

decisions.choice: wilderness: dry, thinly settled country, used for grazing
decisions.reason: The word names land with too little rain for farming, where flocks could still be grazed (Exodus 3:1). It is not only sand desert. The Hebrew name of the book, "In the wilderness", comes from this verse.

decisions.choice: in the tent of meeting: the LORD now speaks from the tabernacle
decisions.reason: At Sinai God first spoke from the mountain (Exodus 19-20). Once the tent was set up, he met Moses there, speaking from above the ark (Exodus 25:22; 40:34-35; Numbers 7:89).

decisions.choice: after the people of Israel came out / left
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "their going out", meaning Israel's. Balanced and Readable name the people so the date is clear.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ("El SEÑOR" at a sentence start, "del SEÑOR", "al SEÑOR")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as in Genesis and Exodus: the divine name is written "el SEÑOR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", and the divine name setting gives "Yahvé". The span takes in the article and its contraction so both options read naturally. "Jehová", the form of the Reina-Valera tradition, is the alternative a Spanish reviewer may prefer. "Lord GOD" (Adonai and the name) is "Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}".

decisions.choice: "el desierto del Sinaí"; "la Tienda del Encuentro"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as the Pentateuch terms list sets: the wilderness is "el desierto" at every level (m2: dry grazing land, not only sand), and the tent of meeting is "la Tienda del Encuentro", which names the tent by its purpose, the meeting of the LORD with Moses (m3).

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ("Le SEIGNEUR" at a sentence start, "du SEIGNEUR", "au SEIGNEUR")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as in Genesis and Exodus: the divine name is written "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD" and the Spanish "el SEÑOR", and the divine name setting gives "Yahvé", the usual French form of the name. The span takes in the article and its contraction. "L'Éternel", used since the Reformation in French Protestant Bibles, is the alternative a reviewer may prefer. "Lord GOD" (Adonai and the name) is "le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}".

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("parla", "il dit"); passé composé at Readable ("a parlé", "il lui a dit"); the LORD's instructions in the future or present at Literal and Balanced ("vous recenserez"), "vous devez" or the imperative at Readable
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as the French style guide and the Pentateuch terms list set: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative; the passé composé is the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. Much of Numbers is instruction, which takes the ordinary French forms for commands.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as in Genesis and Exodus: the divine name is written "BWANA" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", and the divine name setting gives "Yahwe". "Yehova", the form used in some older Swahili writing, is an alternative a reviewer may prefer. "Lord GOD" (Adonai and the name) is "Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}".

decisions.choice: "nyika ya Sinai" (L, B), "jangwa la Sinai" (R, "Desert of Sinai"); "Hema la Kukutania"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers: the Pentateuch terms list allows both "jangwa" and "nyika" for the wilderness. "Nyika" is open grazing country, which is what the word means here (m2), so Literal and Balanced use it; Readable follows the English "Desert" with "jangwa". The tent of meeting is "Hema la Kukutania" at every level, as the terms list sets.

decisions.choice: "광야" for the wilderness at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "Desert", but the meaning decision describes thinly settled grazing country rather than sand desert; "광야" is the ordinary Korean word for it and keeps "시내 광야" one name through Numbers.

decisions.choice: "hoang mạc Si-na-i" and "Lều Hội Kiến" at every level; "phán" for God speaking
alternatives: "lều gặp gỡ" at Readable, as the English Readable says "meeting tent"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch term sheet's words, as Exodus and Leviticus use them: "hoang mạc" is dry, thinly settled grazing land rather than a sand desert, and the one tent keeps one name at every level. "phán" stays the verb for God speaking. Recorded once for Numbers 1-5.

decisions.choice: "tháng thứ hai" for the second month
decisions.reason: "tháng hai" would be read as February in the solar calendar; "tháng thứ hai" keeps Israel's own count of months.

decisions.choice: o deserto do Sinai; a tenda do encontro (every level); os israelitas (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Exodus and Leviticus (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md): "deserto" is the usual Portuguese word for this dry grazing land (m2), lowercase, as in "o deserto do Sinai"; "a tenda do encontro" is already plain Portuguese, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "the meeting tent". Balanced and Readable name the people as "os israelitas", as the English supplies "the people of Israel".

decisions.choice: For the whole of Numbers: the divine name is "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}" at every level; Elohim is "አምላክ" ("God", "the God of ...", "my God") or "እግዚአብሔር" where the one God is meant and YHWH does not stand beside it; "the tent of meeting" is "የመገናኛው ድንኳን" and "the wilderness" "ምድረ በዳ" at every level.
alternatives: "ምድረ በዳ" only at Literal, "በረሃ" at Readable
decisions.reason: As in Genesis to Leviticus, so that the five books read as one. "ጌታ" is kept for Adonai. "ምድረ በዳ" is the ordinary word for open, dry grazing country and is clear at Readable too; "በረሃ" suggests sand desert.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of Numbers.
alternatives: marking pronouns for God with a setting
decisions.reason: The English can capitalise pronouns for God (as in 1:53 at Readable); the Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change in Amharic.

decisions.choice: lift up the head: take a census, count
decisions.reason: To "lift up the head" of a group is to count it (Exodus 30:12). The same phrase returns in verse 49 and 26:2. The command is plural: it is addressed to Moses and Aaron together (verse 3).

decisions.choice: clans and the house of their fathers: the divisions within each tribe
decisions.reason: Israel was made up of tribes, each tribe of clans, and each clan of "fathers' houses", large families named after a common forefather. Joshua 7:14-18 goes down the same steps: tribe, clan, household, man. The census was taken through these family groups.

decisions.choice: by their skulls: one by one, head by head
decisions.reason: The word means "skull". "By the skull" is the way of saying "per head" (Exodus 16:16; 38:26): every male was counted one at a time, by name.

decisions.choice: ancestral families / families
decisions.reason: "House of their fathers" means a family group named after its forefather. Balanced says "ancestral families" and Readable "families"; Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Levanten|Levantad}}, {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}}, {{plural_you:Cuenten|Contad}}
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as in Genesis and Exodus: wherever several people are addressed, the "ustedes" form of Latin America is the default and the plural_you setting gives the "vosotros" form of Spain, on the pronoun and on the verb. Here the command is plural, to Moses and Aaron together (m1).

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L); "los israelitas" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as the Pentateuch terms list sets: the phrase means the whole people. Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters, so the Literal "los hijos de Israel" is inclusive as it stands, and Balanced and Readable say "los israelitas"; Spanish has no second wording for the gender setting to change. Where the phrase means only Jacob's own sons, "hijos de Israel" is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël (L); les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} (B, R)
alternatives: les fils d'Israël without a setting
les enfants d'Israël at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as in Exodus: the phrase means the whole people, women as well as men, so the default is inclusive, as in English: "les enfants d'Israël" at Literal, keeping the Hebrew "sons" as a family word, and "les Israélites" at Balanced and Readable. The gender setting gives the traditional "les fils d'Israël". The census itself counts only men ("tout mâle").

decisions.choice: "la communauté"; "selon leurs clans, selon la maison de leurs pères, selon le nombre des noms" (L); "par clans et par familles" (B, R)
alternatives: "selon leurs familles, selon les maisons de leurs pères"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as the Pentateuch terms list sets: the congregation (the people as one body) is "la communauté", keeping "l'assemblée" for the other Hebrew word. The census formula keeps the three Hebrew phrases at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "par clans et par familles", with "clan" for the clan and "famille" for the father's house (m2). The same wording is used in chapters 2, 3, 4 and 26.

decisions.choice: "wana wa Israeli" (L); "Waisraeli" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as the Pentateuch terms list sets: the phrase means the whole people. Swahili "wana" is not limited to sons, so the Literal keeps it, and Balanced and Readable say "Waisraeli". Swahili has no second wording for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: "jumuiya"; "kwa koo zao, kwa nyumba ya baba zao, kwa hesabu ya majina" (L); "kwa koo na jamaa" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers, as the Pentateuch terms list sets: the congregation is "jumuiya", keeping "kusanyiko" for the assembly. The census formula keeps the three Hebrew phrases at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "kwa koo na jamaa", "ukoo" (plural "koo") for the clan and "jamaa" for the father's house (m2). The count itself is "hesabu" and "kuhesabu", the common words, rather than the loanword "sensa".

decisions.choice: "tính đầu người" (count heads) for "lift up the head" at Literal
alternatives: "kiểm tra dân số" as at Balanced
decisions.reason: Word for word, "nâng đầu" would be heard as raising someone's spirits or honouring them; "tính đầu người" keeps the word "head" and says what the idiom means, a count. Used for the same idiom through these chapters (1:49; 4:2, 22).

decisions.choice: "hội chúng con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L), "hội chúng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B), "cộng đồng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (R), with no gender span; "gia tộc" for clans and "nhà cha" (L) / "gia đình" (B, R) for the house of the fathers
alternatives: a gender span such as "con trai Y-sơ-ra-ên"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch sheet's forms, as in Leviticus. "con cháu" and "dân" already include women and men, so Vietnamese has no second wording for the gender setting; Readable uses the plainer "cộng đồng" as Leviticus does. Book-wide for Numbers 1-5.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (Literal), "이스라엘 백성" (Balanced), "이스라엘 사람들" (Readable) for "the sons of Israel", with no gender span; God's instructions to Moses in 해라체 (-하라, -하지 말라 at Literal and Balanced; -해야 한다, -하면 안 된다 at Readable)
decisions.reason: Book-wide choice for Numbers, as the Pentateuch term sheet sets it. The Korean words already include women and men, so the gender setting has nothing to change and the Korean has no span where the English has one. God speaks to Moses in the plain style, as in Genesis to Leviticus.

decisions.choice: "머릿수를 세다" for "lift up the head" at Literal; "머리 하나하나대로" for "by their skulls"
decisions.reason: A word-for-word "머리를 들다" means to raise one's head (to take courage) in Korean, not to count; "머릿수" keeps the word "head" while saying what the idiom means, as the meaning decision explains. "가문" is the clan and "조상의 집" (Literal) / "집안" (Balanced, Readable) the house of the fathers, as the term sheet sets.

decisions.choice: Levantem a cabeça (L); Façam o recenseamento (B); Contem (R); recensear, os recenseados for the verb "enroll" (verse 3)
decisions.reason: For the whole book. Literal keeps the idiom "lift up the head" (m1), as Exodus 30:12 does in Portuguese; Balanced says "fazer o recenseamento" and Readable "contar", the levels of the English "take a census" and "count". The verb the English renders "enroll" (verse 3) and its participle "those enrolled" (verse 21) are "recensear" and "os recenseados" at Literal and Balanced, the Portuguese words for a census, which Numbers is about; Readable says "contar" and "foram contados". The command is plural, to Moses and Aaron (m1), so the verbs are "vocês" forms.

decisions.choice: segundo os seus clãs, segundo as suas famílias (L); por clãs e por famílias (B); por clãs e famílias (R); todo homem
alternatives: segundo a casa dos seus pais (L)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "clã" names the division of a tribe and "família" the "house of the fathers" (m2), as docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md sets them; Literal does not keep "casa dos seus pais", which in Portuguese reads as a building or the parents' home. The Hebrew word for "male" is "homem" here: Portuguese "macho" is said of animals and "varão" is archaic, and those counted are men of twenty and over (verse 3).

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L); os israelitas (B, R); no gender setting
alternatives: os filhos e as filhas de Israel, under a gender setting
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as Exodus 1:7 and Leviticus 1:2 set it: the English needs a gender setting because "sons" names only men, but Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters and "os israelitas" names the whole people, so a setting would change nothing.

decisions.choice: For the whole book: "ማኅበሩ" for the congregation (ʿedah); "ነገድ" for the tribe; "ጎሳ" for the clan; "በየአባቶቻቸው ቤት" (L) and "በየቤተሰባቸው" (B, R) for "by the house of their fathers"; "ራስ ቁጠሩ" (L) and "ቁጠሩ" (B, R) for "lift up the head".
decisions.reason: The terms list for the Pentateuch sets these; Exodus 30:12 has "ራስ ... ስታነሣ" at Literal. "ቤተሰብ" is the natural word for the ancestral family; Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the fathers' house.

decisions.choice: "የእስራኤል ልጆች" (L, B) and "እስራኤላውያን" (R), with no gender span.
alternatives: a gender span with "የእስራኤል ወንዶችና ሴቶች ልጆች"
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Exodus: "ልጆች" already includes daughters and "እስራኤላውያን" names the whole people, so a setting would change nothing. The census itself counts only men, and the text says so ("ወንድ").

source.text: מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה כָּל־יֹצֵ֥א צָבָ֖א בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל תִּפְקְד֥וּ אֹתָ֛ם לְצִבְאֹתָ֖ם אַתָּ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: From a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army in Israel, you will enroll them by their armies, you and Aaron.

en.L: From a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army in Israel, you will enroll them by their armies, you and Aaron.
en.B: You and Aaron are to enroll them by their divisions, all the men in Israel twenty years old and up, everyone who can go out to war.
en.R: You and Aaron must count every man in Israel who is twenty years old or older and can go out to war. List them by their troops.

es.L: Desde [la edad de] veinte años en adelante, todo el que sale al ejército en Israel, los {{plural_you:alistarán|alistaréis}} por sus ejércitos, tú y Aarón.
es.B: Tú y Aarón {{plural_you:alistarán|alistaréis}} por divisiones a todos los hombres de Israel de veinte años o más, a todos los que son aptos para salir a la guerra.
es.R: Tú y Aarón {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} contar a todos los hombres de Israel que tengan veinte años o más y puedan ir a la guerra. {{plural_you:Anótenlos|Anotadlos}} por tropas.

fr.L: Depuis [l’âge de] vingt ans et au-dessus, tout [homme] qui sort à l’armée en Israël, vous les recenserez selon leurs armées, toi et Aaron.
fr.B: Toi et Aaron, vous recenserez par divisions tous les hommes d’Israël âgés de vingt ans et plus, tous ceux qui peuvent partir à la guerre.
fr.R: Toi et Aaron, vous devez compter tous les hommes d’Israël qui ont vingt ans ou plus et qui peuvent partir à la guerre. Inscrivez-les par troupes.

sw.L: Kuanzia mwana wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, kila atokaye [kwenda] jeshini katika Israeli, mtawaandikisha kwa majeshi yao, wewe na Haruni.
sw.B: Wewe na Haruni mtawaandikisha kwa vikosi vyao wanaume wote wa Israeli wenye umri wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, kila mmoja anayefaa kwenda vitani.
sw.R: Wewe na Haruni lazima mhesabu kila mwanamume katika Israeli mwenye miaka ishirini au zaidi anayeweza kwenda vitani. Waandikeni kwa vikosi vyao.

vi.L: Từ [người] hai mươi tuổi trở lên, mọi người đi ra [nhập] quân đội trong Y-sơ-ra-ên, các ngươi sẽ kiểm kê họ theo các đạo quân của họ, ngươi và A-rôn.
vi.B: Con và A-rôn phải kiểm kê họ theo từng đội quân: mọi người nam trong Y-sơ-ra-ên từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên, tức là mọi người có thể ra trận.
vi.R: Con và A-rôn phải đếm mọi người nam trong Y-sơ-ra-ên từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên có thể ra trận. Hãy ghi tên họ theo từng đội quân.

ko.L: 스무 살 된 아들부터 그 이상으로, 이스라엘에서 군대에 나가는 모든 자를, 너와 아론은 그들의 군대별로 계수하여라.
ko.B: 너와 아론은 이스라엘에서 스무 살 이상으로 전쟁에 나갈 수 있는 모든 남자를 부대별로 계수하여라.
ko.R: 너와 아론은 이스라엘에서 스무 살 이상으로 전쟁에 나갈 수 있는 남자를 모두 세어야 한다. 그들을 부대별로 명단에 올려야 한다.

pt.L: De vinte anos para cima, todo o que sai [para o] exército em Israel, vocês os recensearão segundo os seus exércitos, tu e Arão.
pt.B: Tu e Arão recensearão segundo as suas divisões todos os homens de Israel de vinte anos para cima, aptos para a guerra.
pt.R: Tu e Arão devem contar cada homem de Israel que tem vinte anos ou mais e pode ir à guerra. Registrem os homens por tropas.

am.L: ከሃያ ዓመት ልጅ ጀምሮ ከዚያም በላይ ያሉትን፣ በእስራኤል [ወደ] ሠራዊት የሚወጡትን ሁሉ፣ አንተና አሮን በየሠራዊታቸው ትቆጥሯቸዋላችሁ።
am.B: አንተና አሮን በእስራኤል ያሉትን፣ ዕድሜያቸው ሃያ ዓመትና ከዚያ በላይ የሆነውንና ለጦርነት መውጣት የሚችሉትን ወንዶች ሁሉ በየክፍለ ሠራዊታቸው መዝግቧቸው።
am.R: አንተና አሮን በእስራኤል ያለውን፣ ዕድሜው ሃያ ዓመት ወይም ከዚያ በላይ የሆነውንና ለጦርነት መውጣት የሚችለውን ወንድ ሁሉ መቁጠር አለባችሁ። በየጭፍራቸው መዝግቧቸው።

decisions.choice: every one going out to the army: every man fit for military service
decisions.reason: The word translated "army" means a host or a body of men on service, most often in war. "Going out" is the regular verb for marching out to battle (Deuteronomy 20:1). The count is of men able to fight, from the age of twenty up (Exodus 30:14; 38:26).

decisions.choice: enroll: count and register for service
decisions.reason: The verb means to look after, to take note of, and so to muster or enroll men for a task. It is the key verb of the chapter (verses 19, 44) and is used again in verse 50 in the sense "appoint".

decisions.choice: by their armies: by their military divisions
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for army here means the companies or divisions into which the men were grouped, as in 2:3-31, where each tribe camps "by its armies".

decisions.choice: You and Aaron are to enroll them ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "you and Aaron" at the end for emphasis. Balanced and Readable name them first, as English does, and put the age and the purpose after.

decisions.choice: all the men / every man; divisions / troops
decisions.reason: Those counted are the males of verse 2, so Balanced and Readable say "men". The army units are "armies" at Literal, "divisions" at Balanced and "troops" at Readable, here and through the book.

decisions.choice: "todo el que sale al ejército" (L); "aptos para salir a la guerra" (B); "puedan ir a la guerra" (R); the verb "alistar" for "enroll"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers: the formula for those counted, "every male twenty years old and upward who can go out to war", keeps "sale al ejército" at Literal and says "salir a la guerra" at Balanced and Readable. "Alistar" is the verb for enrolling men for service, which is what the Hebrew verb means here (m2); Readable uses "contar", as the English says "count". The army units are "ejércitos" (L), "divisiones" (B), "tropas" (R).

decisions.choice: "tout [homme] qui sort à l'armée" (L); "tous ceux qui peuvent partir à la guerre" (B, R); the verb "recenser" for "enroll"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers: the formula for those counted, "every male twenty years old and upward who can go out to war", keeps the Hebrew "sort à l'armée" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say plainly "partir à la guerre". "Recenser" is the verb for registering men in a count, and keeps the link between "enroll" and "those enrolled" ("les recensés"); Readable uses "compter", as the English says "count". The army units are "armées" (L), "divisions" (B), "troupes" (R).

decisions.choice: "kila atokaye [kwenda] jeshini" (L); "anayefaa kwenda vitani" (B); "anayeweza kwenda vitani" (R); the verb "kuandikisha" for "enroll"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers: the formula for those counted, "every male twenty years old and upward who can go out to war", keeps "atokaye jeshini" at Literal and says "kwenda vitani" at Balanced and Readable. "Kuandikisha" (to register, enroll) gives the sense of the Hebrew verb (m2), with "walioandikishwa" for "those enrolled"; Readable uses "kuhesabu", as the English says "count". The army units are "majeshi" (L) and "vikosi" (B, R).

decisions.choice: "계수하다" for "enroll" (Literal, Balanced), "세다" at Readable; "군대" (Literal) / "부대" (Balanced, Readable) for "armies"
decisions.reason: "계수하다" is the Korean word for counting people in a census and is used in Exodus 38:25-26 for the same count; Readable uses the everyday verb. The plural "armies" is the military divisions of each tribe, which Korean calls "부대".

decisions.choice: "từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên" for "from a son of twenty years and upward"; "kiểm kê" (L, B) / "đếm" (R) for the enrolling
alternatives: "từ con trai hai mươi năm" at Literal
decisions.reason: Vietnamese states an age with "tuổi"; a word-for-word "son of" would read as a real son. "kiểm kê" is the count-and-register word Exodus 38 already uses for this census; Readable says plainly "đếm". Book-wide for these chapters.

decisions.choice: God calls Moses "ngươi" (L) and "con" (B, R); Moses and Aaron together "các ngươi" (L), "các con" (B), "hai con" (R)
decisions.reason: The Genesis and Pentateuch sheets: God speaking to Moses, Aaron or one person is "ngươi" at Literal, keeping the bare Hebrew "you", and "con" at Balanced and Readable, the close relation of God to his servant; God's laws to Israel keep "các ngươi" at every level. Book-wide for Numbers.

decisions.choice: todo o que sai [para o] exército (L); aptos para a guerra (B); pode ir à guerra (R); exércitos / divisões / tropas
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the phrase means men fit to march out to battle (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced says "apto(s) para a guerra", the usual Portuguese for fitness for military service, and Readable the plainer "pode ir à guerra". The units are "exércitos" (L), "divisões" (B) and "tropas" (R), as the English "armies", "divisions", "troops" (m3).

decisions.choice: vocês ... tu e Arão (L); Tu e Arão recensearão / devem (B, R)
decisions.reason: God speaks to Moses with "tu", and the verb is plural because Aaron is included. Brazilian Portuguese puts a plural subject such as "tu e Arão" with the third person plural verb ("recensearão", "devem"), since the "vós" form is not used; "você e Arão" would change God's address to Moses.

decisions.choice: "በየሠራዊታቸው" (L), "በየክፍለ ሠራዊታቸው" (B), "በየጭፍራቸው" (R) for "by their armies"; "[ወደ] ሠራዊት የሚወጣ" (L) and "ለጦርነት መውጣት የሚችል" (B, R) for "going out to the army".
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses the word for "army" of each tribe's fighting men. Amharic "ሠራዊት" suggests a whole national army, so Balanced speaks of divisions and Readable of troops, as the English does; these hold through chapters 1, 2 and 10.

source.text: וְאִתְּכֶ֣ם יִהְי֔וּ אִ֥ישׁ אִ֖ישׁ לַמַּטֶּ֑ה אִ֛ישׁ רֹ֥אשׁ לְבֵית־אֲבֹתָ֖יו הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And with you will be a man, a man for the tribe; a man [who is] head of [the] house of his fathers [is] he.

en.L: And with you there will be a man, a man for [each] tribe, a man who [is] head of the house of his fathers.
en.B: One man from each tribe is to be with you, each of them the head of his ancestral family.
en.R: One man from each tribe will work with you. Each one will be the leader of his family group.

es.L: Y con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} estará un hombre, un hombre por [cada] tribu, un hombre [que es] cabeza de la casa de sus padres.
es.B: Con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} estará un hombre de cada tribu, cada uno jefe de su familia.
es.R: Un hombre de cada tribu trabajará con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Cada uno será el jefe de su grupo familiar.

fr.L: Et avec vous il y aura un homme, un homme par [chaque] tribu, un homme [qui est] chef de la maison de ses pères.
fr.B: Un homme de chaque tribu sera avec vous, chacun d’eux chef de sa famille.
fr.R: Un homme de chaque tribu travaillera avec vous. Chacun sera le chef de son groupe familial.

sw.L: Na pamoja nanyi atakuwa mtu, mtu kwa [kila] kabila, mtu [aliye] mkuu wa nyumba ya baba zake.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja kutoka kila kabila atakuwa pamoja nanyi, kila mmoja akiwa mkuu wa jamaa yake.
sw.R: Mtu mmoja kutoka kila kabila atafanya kazi pamoja nanyi. Kila mmoja atakuwa kiongozi wa jamaa yake.

vi.L: Và cùng với các ngươi sẽ có một người, một người cho [mỗi] chi tộc, một người [là] đứng đầu nhà cha mình.
vi.B: Mỗi chi tộc phải có một người ở cùng các con, là người đứng đầu gia đình tổ tiên mình.
vi.R: Mỗi chi tộc sẽ có một người làm việc với hai con. Người ấy là người lãnh đạo trong dòng họ mình.

ko.L: 그리고 너희와 함께 지파마다 한 사람, 한 사람이 있을 것인데, 그는 자기 조상의 집의 우두머리인 사람이다.
ko.B: 각 지파에서 한 사람씩 너희와 함께 있게 하여라. 그들은 저마다 자기 집안의 우두머리여야 한다.
ko.R: 지파마다 한 사람씩 너희와 함께 일할 것이다. 그들은 저마다 자기 집안의 지도자이다.

pt.L: E com vocês haverá um homem, um homem de [cada] tribo, um homem que [é] chefe da sua família.

decisions.choice: stand with you: assist you, serve beside you
decisions.reason: To "stand with" someone is to support or help them. The twelve men are not counted themselves as a separate group; they help Moses and Aaron carry out the count.

decisions.choice: the order of the tribes: by the mothers of Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: The list in verses 5-15 starts with the sons of Leah (Reuben, Simeon, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun), then the sons of Rachel (Joseph, counted as Ephraim and Manasseh, and Benjamin), then the sons of the servant women Bilhah and Zilpah (Dan, Asher, Gad, Naphtali) (Genesis 35:23-26). Levi is left out (verses 47-49).

decisions.choice: Elizur, Shedeur: names that speak of God
decisions.reason: Several leaders' names are formed with a word for God: El ("God"), Shaddai ("the Almighty") or Zur ("rock"). Elizur probably means "my God is a rock". The same names return in 2:10, 7:30 and 10:18.

decisions.choice: the leaders' names in their usual Spanish forms: Elisur, Sedeur, Selumiel, Zurisadai, Naasón, Aminadab, Natanael, Zuar, Eliab, Helón, Elisama, Amiud, Gamaliel, Pedasur, Abidán, Gedeoni, Ahiezer, Amisadai, Paguiel, Ocrán, Eliasaf, Deuel, Ahira, Enán
alternatives: closer transcriptions of the Hebrew (Elitsur, Shedeur, Najshón...)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers (the same men return in chapters 2, 7 and 10): Spanish names follow the forms long used in Spanish Bibles, with Spanish accents. Naasón and Aminadab are the forms used in Exodus 6:23 and Matthew 1:4.

decisions.choice: the leaders' names in French transcription: Élitsour, Shedéour, Shéloumiel, Tsourishaddaï, Nahshôn, Netanel, Tsouar, Éliab, Hélon, Élishama, Ammihoud, Gamaliel, Pedahtsour, Abidân, Guidéoni, Ahiézer, Ammishaddaï, Paguiel, Okrân, Éliasaph, Déuel, Ahira, Énân
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers (the same men return in chapters 2, 7 and 10): names with no established French form are transcribed from the Hebrew as the names of Genesis and Exodus are, with "ts" for tsade, "sh" for shin, "ou" for the u sound and French accents. Nahshôn and Amminadab keep the forms used in Exodus 6:23.

decisions.choice: the leaders' names in Swahili form: Elisuri, Shedeuri, Shelumieli, Surishadai, Nashoni, Aminadabu, Nethaneli, Suari, Eliabu, Heloni, Elishama, Amihudi, Gamalieli, Pedasuri, Abidani, Gideoni, Ahiezeri, Amishadai, Pagieli, Okrani, Eliasafu, Deueli, Ahira, Enani

decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers (the same men return in chapters 2, 7 and 10): names end in a vowel where Swahili writes one, with "s" for tsade and "sh" for shin, as in Genesis 36 and 46. Nashoni and Aminadabu are the forms used in Exodus 6:23.

decisions.choice: Names in their established Protestant Korean forms: "엘리술", "스데울", "슬루미엘", "수리삿대", "나손", "아미나답", "느다넬", "수알", "엘리압", "헬론", "엘리사마", "암미훗", "가말리엘", "브다술", "아비단", "기드오니", "아히에셀", "암미삿대", "바기엘", "오그란", "엘리아삽", "드우엘", "아히라", "에난"

decisions.reason: Korean needs the word "지파" to make the tribe the place each leader comes from; the Literal keeps the bare name.

decisions.reason: "con trai" is the form Genesis and Exodus use in genealogies. Names not yet used elsewhere in the Vietnamese follow the usual Protestant spelling and stay the same through Numbers.

decisions.choice: Elizur, filho de Sedeur, and the forms of verses 6-15
decisions.reason: For the whole book, where the twelve leaders first appear (they return in 2, 7 and 10): the usual Brazilian forms, with "s" for sh, "f" for ph, "-ã"/"-om" for a final -an/-on and "-be" after a final b: Elizur, filho de Sedeur (Rúben); Selumiel, filho de Zurisadai (Simeão); Naassom, filho de Aminadabe (Judá); Natanael, filho de Zuar (Issacar); Eliabe, filho de Helom (Zebulom); Elisama, filho de Amiúde (Efraim); Gamaliel, filho de Pedazur (Manassés); Abidã, filho de Gideoni (Benjamim); Aiezer, filho de Amisadai (Dã); Pagiel, filho de Ocrã (Aser); Eliasafe, filho de Deuel (Gade); Aira, filho de Enã (Naftali). alternatives: spelling the names afresh from the Hebrew in each chapter
decisions.reason: One spelling of each name for the whole book, so that the lists in chapters 2, 7 and 10 match this one. Nahshon and Amminadab follow Exodus 6:23 ("ነአሶን", "አሚናዳብ"); Reuel in 2:14 follows Exodus 2:18 ("ራጉኤል").

decisions.choice: the called ones: the marginal reading
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew spells this word in a slightly different way; the Masoretes' marginal reading gives the usual form of "called ones". The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the called ones of the congregation: men summoned to act for the people
decisions.reason: They are chosen representatives, called by name (verse 17). Similar titles are given to the leaders who rise up with Korah (16:2) and to Dathan and Abiram (26:9).

decisions.choice: the thousands of Israel: the large family groups within the tribes
decisions.reason: The word usually means "thousand", but it can also name a unit within a tribe, a clan or division. Gideon says "my thousand is the weakest in Manasseh" (Judges 6:15), and Israel stands before the LORD "by your tribes and by your thousands" (1 Samuel 10:19). Here it stands beside "tribes" and names the groups these men led. On the word in the census totals, see the note at verse 21.

decisions.choice: clans
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "thousands" are here, divisions of a tribe. "Clans" gives that sense, though it is not the word for "clans" used in verse 2. Literal keeps "thousands".

decisions.choice: "los jefes de las tribus" for the leaders (nasi'); "cabeza" (L) and "jefe" (B, R) for a head (rosh) of a family or clan
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers: the leaders of the tribes are "los jefes de las tribus", plain Spanish for the men who lead and represent each tribe (verses 4, 44; chapters 2, 7, 10). "Príncipe" suggests royalty, which the Hebrew title does not. Literal keeps "cabeza" for the Hebrew "head"; Readable says "líderes" for the heads of the clans, to avoid repeating "jefes".

decisions.choice: "les chefs des tribus" for the leaders (nasi'); "chef" also for a head (rosh) of a family or clan
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers: the leaders of the tribes are "les chefs des tribus", plain modern French for the men who lead and represent each tribe (verses 4, 44; chapters 2, 7, 10). "Prince" suggests royalty, which the Hebrew title does not. Readable says "les responsables des clans" for the heads of the clans, to avoid repeating "chefs".

decisions.choice: "viongozi wa makabila" for the leaders (nasi'); "wakuu" (singular "mkuu") for the heads (rosh) of families and clans
decisions.reason: For the whole of Numbers: the leaders of the tribes are "viongozi wa makabila", the men who lead and represent each tribe (verses 4, 44; chapters 2, 7, 10). The heads of families and of the "thousands" are "wakuu", so that the two Hebrew titles stay distinct.

decisions.choice: "씨족" for "the thousands" at every level, Literal included
decisions.reason: A word-for-word "천들" is not Korean, and "천부장" would make these men army officers; the meaning decision reads the word as the large family groups within the tribes, so the Literal says that sense too.

decisions.choice: "지도자" for the tribal leader (nasi) through Numbers
decisions.reason: "지도자" is the word Exodus 34:31 and 35:27 and Leviticus 4:22 already use in Korean; "방백" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: "thủ lĩnh" (L, B) / "người lãnh đạo" (R) for the leaders (nasi); "các nghìn [người]" (L) / "các dòng họ" (B, R) for "the thousands"
decisions.reason: "thủ lĩnh" is the word for the nasi through the Pentateuch drafts and Joshua; Readable says "người lãnh đạo" to explain the title. "the thousands" names large family groups, not a count; Literal keeps the number word with the supplied "người", and Balanced and Readable say "dòng họ", keeping "gia tộc" for the clans.

decisions.choice: os milhares (L); os clãs (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word's ordinary sense, "milhares"; Balanced and Readable say "clãs", following the English and m3, though it is not the word for "clans" in verse 2.

decisions.choice: "አለቆች" (L, B) and "መሪዎች" (R) for the leaders (nasiʾ) of the tribes, through the book.
decisions.reason: As Exodus 16:22 and 34:31 have it. "መሳፍንት" now suggests feudal nobility and "ሹማምንት" appointed officials, while these men are heads of their own tribes.

decisions.choice: took these men ... , and they gathered
decisions.reason: Balanced joins this verse to the next with a comma, since the gathering of the people in verse 18 follows directly on Moses and Aaron taking the twelve men.

decisions.choice: declared their descent: had their family line recorded
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root "to bear a child" and is used only here, in a form that means each person had himself listed by descent. Each man was entered under his clan and family.

decisions.choice: on the first day of the second month: the same day the command was given
decisions.reason: Verse 1 gives the same date. The people were gathered at once, on the day the LORD spoke.

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they". Balanced and Readable make clear that the people, not Moses and Aaron, had their descent recorded.

decisions.choice: "khai dòng dõi mình" for "declared their descent"
decisions.reason: Each man stated his family line so that it could be recorded; "khai" is the ordinary word for declaring something for a register.

decisions.choice: "족보를 신고하다" for "declared their descent"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is built on "bear, give birth"; the meaning decision reads it as having one's family line recorded, which Korean says with "족보" (a family record).

decisions.choice: declararam a sua descendência (L); registrou a sua descendência (B)
alternatives: foram inscritos segundo a sua genealogia
decisions.reason: The verb means each man had his line of descent recorded (m1). Literal keeps "declared"; Balanced says "registrou", the ordinary word for being entered in a record. Balanced joins this verse to verse 17 with a lowercase start, as the English does.

decisions.reason: Reuben was Jacob's oldest son (Genesis 29:32; 49:3), so his tribe is counted first, though he lost the firstborn's place of honor (Genesis 35:22; 49:4; 1 Chronicles 5:1-2).

decisions.choice: their generations: their family lines, their records of descent
decisions.reason: The word means "begettings" and so the line of descent from a forefather, as in the "generations" of Genesis (Genesis 5:1; 10:1). Each man was counted under his line (verse 18).

decisions.choice: the heading of each tribe's count; the number follows in the next verse
decisions.reason: Verses 20-43 repeat one pattern for each tribe: a heading that says how the men were counted, then a verse giving the total. Only Reuben's and Simeon's headings spell out "by their heads, every male"; the others shorten the formula with no change in meaning.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: The Hebrew heading is one long phrase that runs on into the number in verse 21. Balanced and Readable make it two complete sentences and give the number its own sentence in verse 21. In the headings that do not repeat "every male", they say "every man", since those counted are the males of verse 2.

decisions.choice: "varón" for "male" where the Hebrew heading says "every male" (verses 2, 20, 22); "hombre" in the shorter headings
decisions.reason: Spanish "varón" names a male person without the animal sense of "macho" and keeps the Hebrew "male" where it stands; the other headings, which do not repeat it, say "hombre", as the English moves from "male" to "man". Balanced and Readable split each heading into two sentences, as the English does, with the preterite "fueron registrados", "fue contado".

decisions.choice: "tout mâle" at Literal; "tout homme" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: "Mâle" keeps the Hebrew word for a male at Literal, as older French Bibles do in lists and laws; in ordinary French it is used mostly of animals, so Balanced and Readable say "tout homme", which here, with "de vingt ans et plus", can only mean the men.

decisions.choice: "dòng dõi" for "their generations" (toledot); Readable leaves it out
decisions.reason: Here the word is a record of descent, not an age group, so the Genesis sheet's "dòng dõi" fits; "thế hệ" would be read as a generation of people.

decisions.choice: "con đầu lòng" (L, B), "con trai cả" (R)
decisions.reason: The sheet's word for firstborn; Readable uses the everyday "con trai cả", as the English Readable says "oldest son".

decisions.choice: The long Hebrew heading split into two Korean sentences, the listing and then the count
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb last, so a heading of eight phrases would leave the reader waiting for the verb; Balanced and Readable close the first sentence after the family lines, as the English does. The Literal keeps one clause that runs into the total in the next verse.

decisions.choice: forty-six thousand five hundred: the word read as the number "thousand"
alternatives: forty-six units (clans or military companies) with five hundred men in all
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary Hebrew word for "thousand", and the text treats these figures as numbers: the twelve totals add up exactly to 603,550 (verse 46), the same figure as the count of men who paid the half shekel (Exodus 38:26), and close to the "about 600,000 men on foot" who left Egypt (Exodus 12:37). The firstborn sons are counted at 22,273 (3:43), which also fits a very large people. But more than 600,000 fighting men implies a whole people of perhaps two million or more in the wilderness, and that is hard to square with other passages, where Israel is smaller than the nations of Canaan (Deuteronomy 7:7) and too few to fill the land at once (Exodus 23:29-30). The same word can name a unit of a tribe, a clan or a military company (verse 16; Judges 6:15; 1 Samuel 10:19). Read that way, Reuben's figure would be forty-six units with five hundred men in all, and the totals would be far smaller. That reading has to treat the sums in verse 46 and 2:32 as a later misunderstanding, so the text as it stands is followed here, and the question is left open.

decisions.choice: those of them enrolled: the men counted for service
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "enroll" (verse 3) and means those who were mustered. Each tribe's total is given in the same words in verses 21-43.

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Simeon, their generations, by their clans, by [the] house of their fathers, its enrolled [men] by [the] number of names, by their skulls, every male from a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army,

en.L: Of the sons of Simeon, their generations, by their clans, by the house of their fathers, its enrolled [men] by the number of names, by their heads, every male from a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army,
en.B: The descendants of Simeon were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every male twenty years old and up who could go out to war was enrolled by name, one by one.
en.R: The descendants of Simeon were listed by clans and families. Every male twenty years old or older who could go out to war was counted by name.

es.L: De los hijos de Simeón, sus generaciones, por sus clanes, por la casa de sus padres, sus alistados por el número de los nombres, por sus cabezas, todo varón desde [la edad de] veinte años en adelante, todo el que sale al ejército,
es.B: Los descendientes de Simeón fueron registrados según sus linajes, por clanes y por familias. Todo varón de veinte años o más apto para salir a la guerra fue alistado por su nombre, uno por uno.
es.R: Los descendientes de Simeón fueron anotados por clanes y familias. Se contó por su nombre a cada varón de veinte años o más que podía ir a la guerra.

fr.L: Des fils de Siméon, leurs générations, selon leurs clans, selon la maison de leurs pères, ses recensés selon le nombre des noms, par leurs têtes, tout mâle depuis [l’âge de] vingt ans et au-dessus, tout [homme] qui sort à l’armée,
fr.B: Les descendants de Siméon furent inscrits selon leurs lignées, par clans et par familles. Tout homme de vingt ans et plus, capable d’aller à la guerre, fut recensé par son nom, un par un.
fr.R: Les descendants de Siméon ont été inscrits par clans et par familles. Tout homme de vingt ans ou plus qui pouvait partir à la guerre a été compté par son nom.

sw.L: Wa wana wa Simeoni, vizazi vyao, kwa koo zao, kwa nyumba ya baba zao, walioandikishwa wao kwa hesabu ya majina, kwa vichwa vyao, kila mwanamume kuanzia mwana wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, kila atokaye [kwenda] jeshini,
sw.B: Wazao wa Simeoni waliandikishwa kwa vizazi vyao, kwa koo na kwa jamaa. Kila mwanamume mwenye umri wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, aliyefaa kwenda vitani, aliandikishwa kwa jina lake, mmoja mmoja.
sw.R: Wazao wa Simeoni waliorodheshwa kwa koo na jamaa. Kila mwanamume wa miaka ishirini au zaidi aliyeweza kwenda vitani alihesabiwa kwa jina.

vi.L: Về con cháu Si-mê-ôn, dòng dõi của họ, theo gia tộc của họ, theo nhà cha họ, những người được kiểm kê của nó theo số tên, theo từng đầu người, mọi người nam từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên, mọi người đi ra [nhập] quân đội,

vi.R: Con cháu Si-mê-ôn được ghi tên theo gia tộc và gia đình. Mọi người nam từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên có thể ra trận đều được đếm và ghi tên.

ko.L: 시므온의 자손들 가운데서는, 그들의 족보대로, 그들의 가문대로, 그들의 조상의 집대로, 그 계수된 자들을 이름의 수대로, 그들의 머리 하나하나대로, 스무 살 된 아들부터 그 이상으로 군대에 나가는 모든 남자를 [세었는데],

pt.L: Dos filhos de Simeão, as suas gerações, segundo os seus clãs, segundo as suas famílias, os seus recenseados segundo o número de nomes, por cabeça, todo homem de vinte anos para cima, todo o que sai [para o] exército,

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Judah, their generations, by their clans, by [the] house of their fathers, by [the] number of names, from a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army,

en.L: Of the sons of Judah, their generations, by their clans, by the house of their fathers, by the number of names, from a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army,
en.B: The descendants of Judah were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name.

es.L: De los hijos de Judá, sus generaciones, por sus clanes, por la casa de sus padres, por el número de los nombres, desde [la edad de] veinte años en adelante, todo el que sale al ejército,
es.B: Los descendientes de Judá fueron registrados según sus linajes, por clanes y por familias. Todo hombre de veinte años o más apto para salir a la guerra fue contado por su nombre.
es.R: Los descendientes de Judá fueron anotados por clanes y familias. Se contó por su nombre a cada hombre de veinte años o más que podía ir a la guerra.

fr.L: Des fils de Juda, leurs générations, selon leurs clans, selon la maison de leurs pères, selon le nombre des noms, depuis [l’âge de] vingt ans et au-dessus, tout [homme] qui sort à l’armée,
fr.B: Les descendants de Juda furent inscrits selon leurs lignées, par clans et par familles. Tout homme de vingt ans et plus, capable d’aller à la guerre, fut recensé par son nom.
fr.R: Les descendants de Juda ont été inscrits par clans et par familles. Tout homme de vingt ans ou plus qui pouvait partir à la guerre a été compté par son nom.

sw.L: Wa wana wa Yuda, vizazi vyao, kwa koo zao, kwa nyumba ya baba zao, kwa hesabu ya majina, kuanzia mwana wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, kila atokaye [kwenda] jeshini,

sw.R: Wazao wa Yuda waliorodheshwa kwa koo na jamaa. Kila mwanamume wa miaka ishirini au zaidi aliyeweza kwenda vitani alihesabiwa kwa jina.

vi.L: Về con cháu Giu-đa, dòng dõi của họ, theo gia tộc của họ, theo nhà cha họ, theo số tên, từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên, mọi người đi ra [nhập] quân đội,

pt.B: Os descendentes de Naftali foram registrados segundo as suas linhagens, por clãs e por famílias. Todo homem de vinte anos para cima, apto para a guerra, foi contado pelo nome.
pt.R: Os descendentes de Naftali foram registrados por clãs e famílias. Todo homem de vinte anos ou mais que podia ir à guerra foi contado pelo nome.

am.L: የንፍታሌም ልጆች፣ ትውልዳቸው በየጎሳቸው፣ በየአባቶቻቸው ቤት፣ በስሞች ቁጥር፣ ከሃያ ዓመት ልጅ ጀምሮ ከዚያም በላይ፣ [ወደ] ሠራዊት የሚወጣ ሁሉ፣
am.B: የንፍታሌም ዘሮች በየትውልዳቸው፣ በየጎሳቸውና በየቤተሰባቸው ተመዘገቡ። ዕድሜው ሃያ ዓመትና ከዚያ በላይ የሆነና ለጦርነት መውጣት የሚችል ወንድ ሁሉ በስሙ ተቆጠረ።
am.R: የንፍታሌም ዘሮች በየጎሳቸውና በየቤተሰባቸው ተመዘገቡ። ዕድሜው ሃያ ዓመት ወይም ከዚያ በላይ የሆነና ለጦርነት መውጣት የሚችል ወንድ ሁሉ በስሙ ተቆጠረ።

decisions.choice: the sons of Naphtali: the heading without "of"
decisions.reason: Naphtali's heading lacks the small word "of" that begins the other headings. The meaning is the same; the heading is as in verse 20.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

source.text: פְּקֻדֵיהֶ֖ם לְמַטֵּ֣ה נַפְתָּלִ֑י שְׁלֹשָׁ֧ה וַחֲמִשִּׁ֛ים אֶ֖לֶף וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵאֽוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Their enrolled of [the] tribe of Naphtali: three and fifty thousand and four hundred.

en.L: those of them enrolled, of the tribe of Naphtali, [were] 53,400.
en.B: The number enrolled from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
en.R: From the tribe of Naphtali, 53,400 men were counted.

es.L: los alistados de ellos, de la tribu de Neftalí, [fueron] 53 400.
es.B: El número de alistados de la tribu de Neftalí fue de 53 400.
es.R: De la tribu de Neftalí se contaron 53 400 hombres.

fr.L: ceux d’entre eux qui furent recensés, de la tribu de Nephtali, [furent] 53 400.
fr.B: Le nombre des recensés de la tribu de Nephtali fut de 53 400.
fr.R: Dans la tribu de Nephtali, on a compté 53 400 hommes.

sw.L: walioandikishwa wao, wa kabila la Naftali, [walikuwa] 53,400.

sw.R: Kutoka kabila la Naftali walihesabiwa wanaume 53,400.

vi.B: Số người được kiểm kê thuộc chi tộc Nép-ta-li là 53.400.
vi.R: Chi tộc Nép-ta-li có 53.400 người được đếm.

ko.L: 납달리 지파에서 그들 가운데 계수된 자는 53,400[명]이었다.
ko.B: 납달리 지파에서 계수된 사람은 53,400명이었다.
ko.R: 납달리 지파에서 센 사람은 53,400명이었다.

pt.L: os recenseados deles, da tribo de Naftali, [foram] 53.400.
pt.B: O número dos recenseados da tribo de Naftali foi 53.400.
pt.R: Da tribo de Naftali, foram contados 53.400 homens.

am.B: ከንፍታሌም ነገድ የተመዘገቡት 53,400 ነበሩ።
am.R: ከንፍታሌም ነገድ 53,400 ወንዶች ተቆጠሩ።

decisions.choice: the total for Naphtali
decisions.reason: As in verse 21; on the size of the numbers, see the note there. With this figure the twelve totals add up to the sum in verse 46.

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה הַפְּקֻדִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ פָּקַ֨ד מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאַהֲרֹן֙ וּנְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר אִ֑ישׁ אִישׁ־אֶחָ֥ד לְבֵית־אֲבֹתָ֖יו הָיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are] the enrolled whom enrolled Moses and Aaron and [the] leaders of Israel, two [and] ten men; a man, one for [the] house of his fathers they were.

en.L: These [are] those enrolled whom Moses and Aaron enrolled, with the leaders of Israel, twelve men; they were one man each for the house of his fathers.
en.B: These are the men enrolled by Moses and Aaron and by the leaders of Israel, twelve men, each representing his ancestral family.
en.R: These are the men Moses and Aaron counted with the help of the twelve leaders of Israel. Each leader stood for his own tribe.

es.L: Estos [son] los alistados que alistaron Moisés y Aarón, con los jefes de Israel, doce hombres; eran un hombre cada uno por la casa de sus padres.
es.B: Estos son los hombres alistados por Moisés y Aarón y por los jefes de Israel, doce hombres, cada uno en representación de su familia.
es.R: Estos son los hombres que Moisés y Aarón contaron con la ayuda de los doce jefes de Israel. Cada jefe representaba a su propia tribu.

fr.L: Ce [sont] là les recensés que recensèrent Moïse et Aaron, avec les chefs d’Israël, douze hommes ; ils étaient un homme chacun pour la maison de ses pères.
fr.B: Tels sont les hommes recensés par Moïse et Aaron et par les chefs d’Israël, douze hommes, chacun représentant sa famille.
fr.R: Voilà les hommes que Moïse et Aaron ont comptés avec l’aide des douze chefs d’Israël. Chaque chef représentait sa propre tribu.

sw.L: Hawa [ndio] walioandikishwa ambao Musa na Haruni waliwaandikisha, pamoja na viongozi wa Israeli, watu kumi na wawili; walikuwa mtu mmoja kwa ajili ya nyumba ya baba zake.
sw.B: Hawa ndio watu walioandikishwa na Musa na Haruni pamoja na viongozi wa Israeli, watu kumi na wawili, kila mmoja akiwakilisha jamaa yake.
sw.R: Hawa ndio watu ambao Musa na Haruni waliwahesabu kwa msaada wa viongozi kumi na wawili wa Israeli. Kila kiongozi aliwakilisha kabila lake.

vi.L: Đây [là] những người được kiểm kê mà Môi-se và A-rôn đã kiểm kê, cùng với các thủ lĩnh của Y-sơ-ra-ên, mười hai người; họ [là] mỗi người một, cho nhà cha mình.
vi.B: Đó là những người được Môi-se, A-rôn và các thủ lĩnh của Y-sơ-ra-ên kiểm kê. Các thủ lĩnh gồm mười hai người, mỗi người đại diện cho dòng họ tổ tiên mình.
vi.R: Đó là những người Môi-se và A-rôn đã đếm, với sự giúp đỡ của mười hai người lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên. Mỗi người lãnh đạo đại diện cho chi tộc của mình.

ko.L: 이들이 계수된 자들이니, 모세와 아론과 이스라엘의 지도자 열두 사람이 계수한 자들이다. 그 지도자들은 각각 자기 조상의 집을 [대표하는] 한 사람씩이었다.
ko.B: 이들은 모세와 아론, 그리고 저마다 자기 집안을 대표하는 이스라엘의 지도자 열두 사람이 계수한 사람들이다.
ko.R: 이들은 모세와 아론이 이스라엘의 지도자 열두 명의 도움을 받아 센 사람들이다. 지도자들은 저마다 자기 지파를 대표했다.

pt.L: Estes [são] os recenseados que Moisés e Arão recensearam, com os líderes de Israel, doze homens; eles eram um homem para cada família dos seus pais.
pt.B: Esses são os homens recenseados por Moisés e Arão e pelos líderes de Israel, doze homens, cada um representando a sua família.
pt.R: Esses são os homens que Moisés e Arão contaram com a ajuda dos doze líderes de Israel. Cada líder representava a sua própria tribo.

am.L: እነዚህ ሙሴና አሮን የእስራኤልም አለቆች፣ አሥራ ሁለት ሰዎች፣ የቆጠሯቸው የተቆጠሩት ናቸው፤ እያንዳንዳቸው ለአባቶቻቸው ቤት አንድ ሰው ነበሩ።
am.B: እነዚህ ሙሴና አሮን የእስራኤልም አለቆች የመዘገቧቸው ናቸው፤ አለቆቹ አሥራ ሁለት ሰዎች ሲሆኑ እያንዳንዳቸው ቤተሰባቸውን ይወክሉ ነበር።
am.R: ሙሴና አሮን በአሥራ ሁለቱ የእስራኤል መሪዎች እርዳታ የቆጠሯቸው ሰዎች እነዚህ ናቸው። እያንዳንዱ መሪ የራሱን ነገድ ይወክል ነበር።

decisions.choice: the house of his fathers: here, the tribe each leader represented
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in the chapter the phrase names a family within a clan (verse 2), but here each of the twelve men stands for the whole tribe he leads (verses 4, 16).

decisions.choice: twelve men: the leaders of verses 5-15
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "two and ten men", the usual way of writing twelve.

decisions.choice: representing / stood for
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "one man for the house of his fathers". Balanced and Readable say what that means: each leader acted for his group.

decisions.choice: his own tribe
decisions.reason: Readable says "tribe" for "the house of his fathers" here, since each leader stood for a whole tribe (m1).

decisions.choice: um homem para cada família dos seus pais (L)
alternatives: um homem pela casa dos seus pais
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "família" for the "house of the fathers", as in verse 2, with "dos seus pais" so the Hebrew phrase still shows; here it stands for the whole tribe (m1), which Readable says, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיִּֽהְי֛וּ כָּל־פְּקוּדֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה כָּל־יֹצֵ֥א צָבָ֖א בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And were all [the] enrolled of [the] sons of Israel by [the] house of their fathers, from a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army in Israel,

en.L: And all those enrolled of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel by the house of their fathers were, from a son of twenty years and upward, every one going out [to the] army in Israel,
en.B: So all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} twenty years old and up, everyone in Israel who could go out to war, were enrolled by their ancestral families.
en.R: All the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who were twenty years old or older and could go out to war were counted by families.

es.L: Y fueron todos los alistados de los hijos de Israel por la casa de sus padres, desde [la edad de] veinte años en adelante, todo el que sale al ejército en Israel,
es.B: Así, todos los israelitas de veinte años o más, todos los de Israel aptos para salir a la guerra, fueron alistados por familias.
es.R: Todos los israelitas que tenían veinte años o más y podían ir a la guerra fueron contados por familias.

fr.L: Et tous les recensés des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël selon la maison de leurs pères furent, depuis [l’âge de] vingt ans et au-dessus, tout [homme] qui sort à l’armée en Israël,
fr.B: Ainsi tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} âgés de vingt ans et plus, tous ceux d’Israël qui pouvaient partir à la guerre, furent recensés selon leurs familles.
fr.R: Tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} qui avaient vingt ans ou plus et qui pouvaient partir à la guerre ont été comptés par familles.

sw.L: Na walioandikishwa wote wa wana wa Israeli kwa nyumba ya baba zao walikuwa, kuanzia mwana wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, kila atokaye [kwenda] jeshini katika Israeli,
sw.B: Basi Waisraeli wote wenye umri wa miaka ishirini na zaidi, kila mmoja katika Israeli aliyefaa kwenda vitani, waliandikishwa kwa jamaa zao.
sw.R: Waisraeli wote waliokuwa na miaka ishirini au zaidi na walioweza kwenda vitani walihesabiwa kwa jamaa zao.

vi.L: Và tất cả những người được kiểm kê của con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên theo nhà cha họ, từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên, mọi người đi ra [nhập] quân đội trong Y-sơ-ra-ên,
vi.B: Vậy, mọi người nam trong dân Y-sơ-ra-ên từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên, tức là mọi người trong Y-sơ-ra-ên có thể ra trận, đều được kiểm kê theo gia đình tổ tiên mình.
vi.R: Mọi người nam trong dân Y-sơ-ra-ên từ hai mươi tuổi trở lên có thể ra trận đều được đếm theo gia đình.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손 가운데 조상의 집대로 계수된 모든 자, 곧 스무 살 된 아들부터 그 이상으로 이스라엘에서 군대에 나가는 모든 자는,
ko.B: 이렇게 하여 이스라엘에서 스무 살 이상으로 전쟁에 나갈 수 있는 이스라엘 백성이 모두 집안별로 계수되었다.
ko.R: 스무 살 이상으로 전쟁에 나갈 수 있는 이스라엘 사람들을 모두 집안별로 세었다.

pt.L: E todos os recenseados dos filhos de Israel, segundo as suas famílias, foram, de vinte anos para cima, todo o que sai [para o] exército em Israel,
pt.B: Assim, todos os israelitas de vinte anos para cima, todos os de Israel aptos para a guerra, foram recenseados segundo as suas famílias.
pt.R: Todos os israelitas de vinte anos ou mais que podiam ir à guerra foram contados por famílias.

am.L: የእስራኤልም ልጆች የተቆጠሩት ሁሉ በየአባቶቻቸው ቤት፣ ከሃያ ዓመት ልጅ ጀምሮ ከዚያም በላይ፣ በእስራኤል [ወደ] ሠራዊት የሚወጣ ሁሉ፣
am.B: ስለዚህ ዕድሜያቸው ሃያ ዓመትና ከዚያ በላይ የሆኑ፣ በእስራኤል ለጦርነት መውጣት የሚችሉ የእስራኤል ልጆች ሁሉ በየቤተሰባቸው ተመዘገቡ።
am.R: ዕድሜያቸው ሃያ ዓመት ወይም ከዚያ በላይ የሆኑና ለጦርነት መውጣት የሚችሉ እስራኤላውያን ሁሉ በየቤተሰባቸው ተቆጠሩ።

decisions.choice: the grand total: verses 45-46 sum up the count
decisions.reason: Verse 45 repeats the terms of the census (verses 2-3) and verse 46 gives the number. The Hebrew says "and were all the enrolled" twice, once at the start of each verse.

decisions.choice: a complete sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable close the sentence here and give the total its own sentence in verse 46.

decisions.choice: 603,550: the same total as in Exodus
decisions.reason: The twelve tribal totals add up to exactly this number. It is the same as the number of men who paid the half shekel when the tabernacle was built (Exodus 38:26), and it is repeated when the camps are arranged (2:32). The second census, near the end of the wilderness years, gives 601,730 (26:51). On the size of these numbers, see the note at verse 21.
The Hebrew writes "six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty". All three levels give it in figures.

decisions.choice: the Levites were not enrolled: their count comes later, and in a different way
decisions.reason: Levi is counted separately in chapter 3, every male from one month old (3:15, 39), and again for the work of carrying the tabernacle, from thirty to fifty (4:2-3, 46-48). They were not counted for war, because their service was at the tabernacle (verses 50-53).

decisions.choice: For / This was because
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the link to verse 47 clear (m1).
